record.original_question: For each complexity class C among VWaring, VChow, and VBP, determine whether the class equals its corresponding border analogue.

evidence.quote: Problem 15. Let C be a complexity class among VWaring, VChow or VBP. Determine whether C = C.
Little is known about the diﬀerence between a complexity class and its border analogue.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background. In algebraic complexity theory, polynomials over a field (taken here to be the complex numbers) are computed by various models, giving rise to complexity classes that consist of (sequences of) polynomials whose computational cost grows polynomially in the input parameters.

(a) The class VBP consists of (sequences of) polynomials computable by polynomial-size algebraic branching programs: directed acyclic graphs with a source s and a sink t whose edges are labeled by affine linear forms in the input variables, the polynomial computed being the sum over all s–t paths of the product of edge labels.

(b) The class VChow consists of polynomials of polynomial Chow rank, i.e. those degree-d homogeneous polynomials f(x_1,...,x_n) expressible as a sum f = ∏_{j=1}^{d} L_{1,j} + ∏_{j=1}^{d} L_{2,j} + ... + ∏_{j=1}^{d} L_{r,j} of r products of d linear forms, with r bounded polynomially in n and d.

(c) The class VWaring consists of polynomials of polynomial Waring rank, i.e. degree-d homogeneous polynomials expressible as a sum f = ∑_{i=1}^{r} L_i^d of r d-th powers of linear forms, with r polynomially bounded.

For each such class C, its border (or approximative) closure C̄ is defined as the class of polynomials f that can be written as a limit (in the Euclidean or Zariski topology, equivalently as the ε→0 limit of polynomials whose coefficients are Laurent polynomials in a formal parameter ε) of polynomials f_ε belonging to C, with the relevant complexity measure of f_ε remaining polynomially bounded uniformly in ε.

Problem. For each C ∈ {VWaring, VChow, VBP}, decide whether C = C̄; i.e., determine whether every polynomial in the border closure of C already lies in C.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent surveys and papers (2024–2025) on debordering describe the equality of these algebraic complexity classes with their border closures as an open central question. Progress has been made on quantitative debordering (e.g., improved upper bounds on Waring rank in terms of border Waring rank such as d·r^{O(√r)}, and fixed-parameter debordering of Waring rank), but no proof of equality (or separation) of VWaring, VChow, or VBP with their respective border analogues has been established.

status_evidence.title: Recent Advances in Debordering Methods
status_evidence.snippet: Debordering is the task of proving an upper bound on some non-border complexity measure in terms of a border complexity measure...
status_evidence.claim: Debordering remains an open research program; equality of classes with border analogues is not established.

status_evidence.title: Improved Debordering of Waring Rank
status_evidence.snippet: If a degree-d homogeneous polynomial f has border Waring rank r, then its Waring rank is bounded by d·r^{O(√r)}.
status_evidence.claim: Only quantitative debordering progress is known for Waring rank; the equality VWaring = VWaring-bar is not proven.

status_evidence.title: Fixed-parameter debordering of Waring rank
status_evidence.snippet: Fixed-parameter debordering results for Waring rank.
status_evidence.claim: Partial debordering results exist but the full equality question remains open.
